raw_response:
I am already looking at the wheat in the field, so I do not start from a blank slate. I farm the way I always have: first make sure the land gives me something dependable, then see how much cash I still have for extra input. On my 10.9 mu, I will keep most of the land in cotton because that is my main cash crop, but I will still keep some wheat and then maize on the same piece of land, so the family has grain and I do not put all my hope on one crop. I cannot gamble much at my age. If I see a crop do well with my own eyes, I follow that. If money is tight, I would rather cut back a little on seed or one spray than let the crop go hungry at the key time.

For wheat, it is already planted from last autumn, so now my job is to carry it through spring with one topdressing and a couple of irrigations if the ground stays dry. After wheat harvest, I will rush to put in summer maize on that same land, no fancy tillage, just quick work so I do not miss moisture. Cotton on the other 6 mu I will manage a bit more carefully because that is where I earn cash, but I still will not go too heavy on spending. I will use what people around here use, round numbers, not too little and not too much. If the year turns dry, I will give water to wheat at jointing and cotton at flowering first, because those times matter most.
